corrected_fields.summary: The Bank of Canada publishes a comprehensive dashboard of capacity and inflation indicators, updated after each policy announcement. The latest data shows CPI inflation at 1.8% year-over-year (Feb 2026), while the output gap is estimated between -0.8% and -1.8% depending on methodology, indicating residual economic slack.
corrected_fields.why_it_matters: This dashboard aggregates the key economic indicators that the Bank of Canada uses to assess capacity pressures and inflation trends for monetary policy decisions. The combination of inflation data, output gap estimates, labour market indicators, and wage measures provides a comprehensive view of Canadian economic conditions. Market participants monitor these indicators to gauge economic health and predict future BoC policy moves.
corrected_fields.macro_context: Canadian economy shows mixed signals: headline CPI at 1.8% with core measures (CPI-trim, CPI-median, CPI-common) between 2.3-2.4%; the output gap suggests residual slack persisting into 2026; wage growth is decelerating from previous highs. Energy price deflation (-12.2%) contrasts with non-energy commodity strength (+19.4%), complicating the inflation outlook. The housing market remains weak with new home prices declining at -2.3%.
